samples.summary: No test covers the `login` action wiring: that the nonce placed in the OAuth URL is the same one bound to the callback server
samples.evidence: login.test.ts only imports and exercises `createLoginNonce`, `nonceMatches` and `startCallbackServer` directly. The action handler at login.ts:34-40 generates the nonce, passes it to `startCallbackServer(nonce)` and interpolates it into `${server}/auth/github?mode=cli&port=${port}&nonce=${nonce}` — that is the whole security contract of the change, and the failure mode it guards against (two different nonces, or the query key spelled differently from what `github-auth.guard.ts` reads via `req.query?.nonce`) leaves every helper test green while every real login is refused for the full timeout. The backend side explicitly added `github-auth.guard.spec.ts` with a comment that the wiring must be pinned because the helper tests hand the nonce in directly; the CLI side of the same wiring got no equivalent test.
searchedFor: grep 'registerLoginCommand|mode=cli|nonce=' across packages/cli (only src hits, no test hits)

samples.summary: Vacuous assertion: `expect(written).not.toContain("'-7")` holds regardless of the neutralization setting
samples.evidence: `-7` matches `PLAIN_NUMBER` in src/output/csv.ts:12, so `neutralizeFormula` returns it untouched even when `neutralizeFormulas: true`. The assertion therefore passes whether or not the export path disables neutralization, and cannot fail for the behavior the test claims to pin. The adjacent `not.toContain("'=SUM(B2:B100)")` is the only assertion in the test that actually discriminates.

samples.summary: The new `neutralizeFormulas: false` branch of `formatCsv` has no direct unit test of quoting/escaping
samples.evidence: Every `formatCsv` case in test/output.test.ts (lines 88-171) passes `{ neutralizeFormulas: true }`. The only exercise of the `false` branch is the sheets-export end-to-end test, whose fixture contains no comma, quote, CR, tab or nested object — so nothing verifies that the interchange path still quotes delimiters/control characters correctly (i.e. that only neutralization, not escaping, was disabled).

samples.summary: The new `code: 'INVALID_FORMAT'` on content/slides/notes format parsers is unasserted by any test
samples.evidence: `parseContentFormat`, `parseNotesContentFormat` and `parseSlidesContentFormat` were switched from a plain `Error` to `InvalidFormatError`. The only tests touching them (docs-content.test.ts:75-76, notes-content.test.ts:43-44, slides-content.test.ts:144-145) assert `toThrow(/Invalid --format/)` on the message, which was already true before the change. The stated point of the change — that `outputError` reports `INVALID_FORMAT` instead of `ERROR` for these — is untested, so reverting these three call sites to `new Error(...)` keeps every test green.

samples.summary: `--format` validation ordering added to docs/notes/slides/sheets-import commands is untested
samples.evidence: New ordering guards (parseOutputFormat before the request) got tests for files (files-format.test.ts), tabs (tabs.test.ts), api-keys (api-keys.test.ts), status/ctx/schema (status.test.ts). The identical change in docs.ts, notes.ts, slides.ts and sheets-import.ts has no test asserting that a bad `--format` short-circuits before the mutation (e.g. `docs delete --format bogus` must not delete). Since the whole justification is 'a rejected format must not discard the response of a write that already happened', the mutating commands in those files are the ones most worth pinning.
searchedFor: read test/files-format.test.ts, test/tabs.test.ts new block, test/status.test.ts

samples.summary: Happy-path `cells batch` test asserts only that fetch was called, not what was sent
samples.evidence: 'sends valid --data JSON to the batch endpoint' asserts `fetchMock` was called once and exitCode 0; it never inspects the URL, method or serialized `cells` body. Since the refactor moved the parse out of the request try-block, an assertion that the parsed `{"A1":{"value":"1"}}` actually reaches the PATCH body would be what pins the refactor didn't drop the payload.

verdict.reason: No test anywhere exercises the `login` action handler. `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts` has exactly two importers repo-wide: `packages/cli/src/cli.ts:10` (production) and `packages/cli/test/login.test.ts:6`, which imports only `createLoginNonce`, `nonceMatches` and `startCallbackServer` and hands the nonce in directly, building the callback URL itself. Nothing asserts the OAuth URL built at login.ts:40, so the contract that the nonce interpolated as `&nonce=` is the same value bound to `startCallbackServer(nonce)` at login.ts:34-35 is unpinned: a mismatched nonce or a query key spelled differently from what `packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts` reads leaves all helper tests green while every real login is refused until timeout. Searched and ruled out: all 31 `packages/cli/test/*.test.ts`, all 14 `packages/backend/test/*.e2e-spec.ts`, greps for `registerLoginCommand|mode=cli|Opening browser`, `auth/github|startCallbackServer|createLoginNonce`, `nonce`, and `nonce=|state=|oauthUrl` under `**/test/**` — zero test hits outside login.test.ts. Indirect routes checked: bin.test.ts mocks `../src/cli.js` wholesale; output.test.ts:587-595 and schema.test.ts:42-95 assert only the command name/schema row. The backend pinned the mirror-image wiring deliberately (github-auth.guard.spec.ts:27-33 comment, assertions at :62-68); the CLI half of the same binding got nothing. Major under the missing-tests lane: a real behavior change with no meaningful test of the wiring itself.

finding.summary: GitHubAuthGuard's nonce wiring is untested — only the pure parseCliNonce helper is covered
finding.evidence: The new github-auth.guard.spec.ts tests only parseCliNonce() in isolation. Nothing exercises GitHubAuthGuard.canActivate(), which is where the change lives (createState(mode, portNum, parseCliNonce(req.query?.nonce)), github-auth.guard.ts:36-40). If the third argument were dropped or read from the wrong query key, every test in the diff would still pass: cli-auth.store.spec.ts:40 passes the nonce directly to createState, and auth.controller.spec.ts:218 likewise constructs the state by hand. The CSRF binding chain (query param -> stored state -> loopback state) has an untested link at its entry point.

verdict.reason: The finding claims github-auth.guard.spec.ts tests only parseCliNonce and that GitHubAuthGuard.canActivate's nonce wiring is untested. The spec file in this working tree contains a dedicated `describe('GitHubAuthGuard.canActivate')` block (lines 34-89) that instantiates the real guard with a stub CliAuthStore and a fake ExecutionContext, stubbing only the inherited passport `canActivate` (lines 41-48) so the guard's own logic still runs. It asserts `createState` is called with ('cli', 49152, nonce) (line 67) — the exact assertion that would fail if the third argument were dropped or read from the wrong query key — plus undefined-nonce/malformed-nonce cases (lines 71-78), the no-state cases for web login and out-of-range/non-numeric ports (lines 80-88), and `req.__cliStateToken` propagation (lines 68, 83). The store signature `createState(mode, port, nonce?)` (cli-auth.store.ts:27-31) matches, so the positional assertion is meaningful, not vacuous. The claimed gap does not exist.
